label: Bayesian likelihood contrast determines binary check accuracy gain
meaning: Use the existing binary-check accuracy certificate on the two conditional posteriors. Adding the joint equations recovers the prior. Eliminating the common pooled prior gives w(1-w)(u-v)=p(1-p)(a-b); substitution into the existing gain identity gives the scaled formula. The nondegenerate weights and prior make the zero-gain condition exactly equality of likelihoods. This real-valued joint-equation profile allows zero likelihoods with positive predictive masses, whereas the earlier contrastive rational Comparison has strictly positive likelihoods. It does not assign actual probabilities, establish reason attribution or supply a threshold of sufficient warrant.
